items.title: 56706_Buddy Tate oral history interview
items.q: So George and I was always tight, you know?

ctx.x: That's when they were having the festival. Well, I played there the first night with Benny Goodman's big band. That was in '58. And, of course, John had made us stay over to play for Billie and me and Pee-wee and Jack T., Georgie Auld and Prez and Buck, Jo Jones. I don't remember who -- Walter Page. That was the rhythm section. I don't remember who we had on piano. So we all stayed there and played for -- I stayed -- as a matter of fact, I did two days, you know. I stayed there and did the -- after Benny's…

So Prez was -- he was sick then. It was getting to him, you know, he was really failing. He was short-winded, he didn't have any stamina, couldn't hardly fill his horn, you know what I mean? Sound -- couldn't control his sound. So that day, we had a rehearsal, rehearsing things with Billie. So George and I was always tight, you know? Georgie always -- I'll show you, on the other hand -- he calls me Miss Tate and
I call him Mrs. Auld. We always -- "Hello, Miss Tate," right now, you know, he'd do it.
